what_it_does: This paper tackles a problem in wireless full-duplex receivers—devices that transmit and receive simultaneously on the same frequency. When you transmit and receive at the same time, your own signal bleeds into your receiver and drowns out the incoming signal. The authors use a technique called Hilbert-transform equalization to mathematically remove this self-interference, using a cascaded chain of allpass filters (circuits that pass all frequencies but adjust their timing). The key innovation is achieving 65 decibels of interference cancellation over a 120 megahertz bandwidth while keeping frequency response flat, a tradeoff that usually forces designers to choose between bandwidth and noise performance.
